observations: A flatbed truck chassis carries a large orange drilling rig mast and mud-pump assembly mounted behind the cab.
Cab badge reads 'NISSAN DIESEL' with a 'UD' emblem, visible in photo 2.
Windscreen is cracked/dirty with a hand-painted note 'BENT PARTS STEERING, NO HAND SIGNAL' taped to the grille in photos 0 and 2, suggesting a known steering/signal fault.
Rig mast, pump housing and hoses show heavy rust, dried mud and corrosion throughout photos 0 and 1.
Tires look worn and mismatched; truck is parked on bare earth among other used heavy equipment (loaders, forklifts), suggesting a scrapyard/dealer lot rather than an active worksite.
No photo shows the engine running, the mast raised and drilling, or the mud pump operating.
No photo shows the engine bay, chassis underside, hydraulic cylinders up close, or compressor tank markings.
License plate is partially visible in photo 2 but not fully legible.

claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the engine running, the mast operating, or the mud pump/compressor engaged; static yard photos only.
This describes sale terms (as-is, delivered to buyer's site) rather than a verifiable technical condition; no supporting documentation shown.

claims.claim: (Implied) steering and signal system fault noted on windshield sign
claims.evidence: Hand-written sign in photos 0 and 2 reading 'BENT PARTS STEERING, NO HAND SIGNAL' contradicts the 'working fine' claim.

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and running, and the drilling mast being raised/lowered with the mud pump circulating water.
Close-up photos of the steering linkage and a short test-drive clip showing steering and turn-signal function.
Close-up photos of the compressor/mud pump nameplate and any manufacturer markings on the rig itself.
Photos of vehicle registration, roadworthiness certificate, and proof of ownership.
Close-up photos of all tires, chassis rails, and mast welds for corrosion/structural assessment.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used Nissan Diesel (UD) truck-mounted borehole drilling rig in visibly rough, unverified mechanical condition, with the seller's own signage flagging a steering fault that contradicts the 'working fine' claim; absent any operational proof, it must be priced at worst case as a non-running, faulty rig.
